claim: With a capacity of 2, after put a, put b, put a again and put c, the key a is still in the cache.
why: Putting an existing key only reassigns its value: the helper moves a key to the end only when the key is new, so a keeps its oldest position and is evicted when c arrives. The README says both get and put mark a key as most recently used, which is true of get and of put for new keys only. The trap is believing the README and seeing move_to_end on the put path, which does not run for an existing key.

deciding.note: put of an existing key does not refresh it

root.claim: After put a, put b, put a, put c at capacity 2, a is still cached.

atoms.claim: Re-putting an existing key makes it most recently used
atoms.evidence: put calls _store, which calls move_to_end only when the key is new; an existing key is only reassigned and keeps its old position, so a stays oldest.

atoms.claim: Putting c at capacity evicts the oldest key, which is a
atoms.evidence: popitem(last=False) removes the first item; a run gives keys b and c after the sequence.
